A Visual Proof That One Layer Can Comput.zh: 一层网络能够计算任意函数的可视化证明
A Visual Proof That One Layer Can Comput.src: A Visual Proof That One Layer Can Compute Anything

The Universal Approximation Theorem says.zh: 通用逼近定理指出，具有@@T0@@单个@@T1@@隐藏层的神经网络可以模拟几乎任意函数。本页逐步重建 Michael Nielsen 优美的可视化论证，一次一个可拖拽的部件——你将把一个 sigmoid 压平为阶跃，把两个阶跃粘合成一个凸包，手工设计整条曲线，再把@@T2@@塔块@@T3@@堆叠成三维曲面。这里没有形式化证明，只有可以拖动的图形。
The Universal Approximation Theorem says.src: The Universal Approximation Theorem says a neural net with a single hidden layer can mimic almost any function. This page rebuilds Michael Nielsen's beautiful visual argument, one grabbable piece at a time—you'll flatten a sigmoid into a step, glue two steps into a bump, design a whole curve by hand, then stack towers into a 3-D surface. No proof. Just pictures you can drag.

The claim that sounds too good.zh: 一个听起来过于美好的论断
The claim that sounds too good.src: The claim that sounds too good

Here is one of the most quoted results i.zh: 这是机器学习中被引用最多的结论之一：只要神经元足够多，具有@@T0@@单个隐藏层@@T1@@的前馈网络就能以@@T4@@任意@@T5@@精度逼近@@T2@@任意@@T3@@连续函数。一层网络，任意函数。人们把它当作口号反复传诵——却几乎没有人能@@T6@@看懂@@T7@@它为何成立。
Here is one of the most quoted results i.src: Here is one of the most quoted results in machine learning: a feed-forward network with a single hidden layer can approximate any continuous function to any accuracy, given enough neurons. One layer. Any function. People repeat it like a slogan—but almost nobody can see why it's true.

We're going to make it visible, followin.zh: 我们将让它变得可见，沿用 Michael Nielsen 在@@T2@@《Neural Networks and Deep Learning》@@T3@@@@T0@@第 4 章@@T1@@中给出的构造。先说明两点必要的限定，因为这个定理比那句口号要稍微狭窄一些：
We're going to make it visible, followin.src: We're going to make it visible, following Michael Nielsen's construction from Chapter 4 of Neural Networks and Deep Learning. Two honest caveats first, because the theorem is a little narrower than the slogan:

@@T0@@Caveat 1 &mdash; approximate, not.zh:
@@T0@@限定 1——是逼近，而非精确。@@T1@@
          我们不能完美地计算一个函数，只能做到@@T2@@任意接近@@T3@@——并且通过增加神经元来缩小差距。
@@T0@@Caveat 1 &mdash; approximate, not.src: Caveat 1 — approximate, not exact. We won't compute a function perfectly. We'll get arbitrarily close—and we shrink the gap by adding more neurons.

@@T0@@Caveat 2 &mdash; continuous functi.zh:
@@T0@@限定 2——仅限连续函数。@@T1@@
          目标函数必须是连续的（没有瞬时跳跃）。这正是单个隐藏层所能处理的那一类函数。
@@T0@@Caveat 2 &mdash; continuous functi.src: Caveat 2 — continuous functions only. The target has to be continuous (no instantaneous jumps). That's the class one hidden layer can handle.

The trick the whole way through: stop th.zh: 贯穿始终的技巧在于：不要再把隐藏层看作“一个网络”，而要把它看作一箱可互换的@@T0@@积木@@T1@@。我们先来锻造第一块积木。
The trick the whole way through: stop th.src: The trick the whole way through: stop thinking of the hidden layer as “a network” and start thinking of it as a kit of interchangeable bricks. Let's forge the first brick.

One sigmoid neuron is an S-curve.zh: 单个 sigmoid 神经元是一条 S 形曲线
One sigmoid neuron is an S-curve.src: One sigmoid neuron is an S-curve

A single hidden neuron with a sigmoid ac.src: A single hidden neuron with a sigmoid activation computes

where $\\sigma(z) = 1/(1 + e^{-z})$ is t.zh: 其中 $\sigma(z) = 1/(1 + e^{-z})$ 是光滑的 S 形 sigmoid 函数。@@T0@@权重 $w$@@T1@@ 控制 S 形的陡峭程度；@@T2@@偏置 $b$@@T3@@ 使它左右平移。这就是该神经元的全部能力——一条柔和的“开/关”斜坡。
where $\\sigma(z) = 1/(1 + e^{-z})$ is t.src: where $\sigma(z) = 1/(1 + e^{-z})$ is the smooth S-shaped sigmoid. The weight $w$ controls how steep the S is; the bias $b$ slides it left and right. That's the neuron's entire repertoire—a single soft “on/off” ramp.

Drag both sliders and watch the curve ti.zh: 拖动两个滑块，观察曲线如何倾斜与平移。
Drag both sliders and watch the curve ti.src: Drag both sliders and watch the curve tilt and slide.

@@T0@@Notice.@@T1@@\n The curve.zh:
@@T0@@请留意。@@T1@@
          这条曲线总是从最左端的 $0$ 升到最右端的 $1$。$|w|$ 越大，过渡越锐利。如果把 $w$ 一直调到 $80$ 会怎样？S 形被挤压成一道竖直的悬崖——一个@@T2@@阶跃@@T3@@。记住这一点，它就是下一步。
@@T0@@Notice.@@T1@@\n The curve.src: Notice. The curve always runs from $0$ on the far left to $1$ on the far right. Bigger $|w|$ makes the transition sharper. What happens if you crank $w$ all the way to $80$? The S squeezes into a vertical cliff — a step. Hold that thought; it's the next move.

Crank the weight &rarr; a step function.zh: 把权重调大 → 得到阶跃函数
Crank the weight &rarr; a step function.src: Crank the weight → a step function

When the weight is enormous, the sigmoid.zh: 当权重极大时，sigmoid 不再像一条柔和的 S 形，而是突变为@@T0@@阶跃函数@@T1@@：左侧为 $0$，右侧为 $1$，中间是一道近乎竖直的悬崖。这是一次极大的简化——一个阶跃只需用单个数字描述：其悬崖的@@T2@@位置@@T3@@。
When the weight is enormous, the sigmoid.src: When the weight is enormous, the sigmoid stops looking like a gentle S and snaps into a step function: $0$ on the left, $1$ on the right, with a near-vertical cliff in between. That's a huge simplification—a step is described by a single number: the position of its cliff.

The cliff sits where the sigmoid's input.zh: 悬崖位于 sigmoid 输入为零之处，即 $wx + b = 0$，故 $x = -b/w$。Nielsen 的关键动作是用这个位置为神经元@@T0@@重新命名@@T1@@。定义阶跃位置
The cliff sits where the sigmoid's input.src: The cliff sits where the sigmoid's input is zero, i.e. $wx + b = 0$, so $x = -b/w$. Nielsen's key move is to rename the neuron by this position. Define the step position

Now we can forget $w$ and $b$ and just s.zh: 现在我们大可忘掉 $w$ 和 $b$，直接说“位于 $s$ 处的阶跃”。下面的第一个滑块@@T0@@直接@@T1@@设定 $s$（它在背后反解出偏置）。第二个滑块则说明为何权重足够大时我们才能把 sigmoid 当作干净的阶跃。
Now we can forget $w$ and $b$ and just s.src: Now we can forget $w$ and $b$ and just say “a step at $s$.” The first slider below sets $s$ directly (it solves for the bias behind the scenes). The second shows why a big weight is what lets us pretend a sigmoid is a clean step.

Slide the steepness up to make a sharp c.zh: 把陡峭度调高以形成锐利的悬崖，再调低，观察它重新融回柔和的 S 形。
Slide the steepness up to make a sharp c.src:
Slide the steepness up to make a sharp cliff, then down to watch it
          melt back into a soft S.

A high-weight sigmoid behaving as a step.zh: 高权重下的 sigmoid 在 $x = s$ 处表现为阶跃。
A high-weight sigmoid behaving as a step.src: A high-weight sigmoid behaving as a step at $x = s$.

@@T0@@The payoff.@@T1@@\n From.zh:
@@T0@@收获。@@T1@@
          自此以后，每个隐藏神经元不过是“位于位置 $s$ 处的一个阶跃”。一个神经元对应一个数字。这就是我们构建其余一切时所使用的词汇。
@@T0@@The payoff.@@T1@@\n From.src: The payoff. From here on, every hidden neuron is just “a step at position $s$.” One number per neuron. That's the vocabulary we build everything else from.

Two steps make a bump.zh: 两个阶跃构成一个凸包

Let's build this one slowly, by stacking.zh: 我们慢慢来，一次叠加一个 sigmoid。下面是一个小型工作台：一份 sigmoid 神经元列表和一个绘图区。每个神经元都以其自身颜色画成一条@@T0@@虚线@@T1@@曲线；@@T2@@橙色@@T3@@线是@@T4@@累计总和@@T5@@——即所有项相加的结果。用 @@T6@@●@@T7@@ 按钮开启或关闭某个神经元，观察总和的变化。
Let's build this one slowly, by stacking.src: Let's build this one slowly, by stacking sigmoids one at a time. Below is a little workbench: a list of sigmoid neurons and a plot. Each neuron is drawn as a dashed curve in its own colour; the orange line is the running total—everything added up. Use the ● button to switch a neuron on or off, and watch the total change.

Start with the two neurons already there.zh: 先看已有的两个神经元，把第二个@@T0@@关闭@@T1@@：只剩下 $s_1$ 处一个@@T2@@上升阶跃@@T3@@，其输出权重为 $+1$。它一旦上升就保持不降——并不局部。现在把第二个重新打开。它是 $s_2$ 处的阶跃，但输出权重为 $-1$，因此是一个@@T4@@下降@@T5@@阶跃。把两者相加：
Start with the two neurons already there.src: Start with the two neurons already there but turn the second one off: you're left with a single rising step at $s_1$, with output weight $+1$. It goes up and stays up—not very local. Now turn the second one back on. It's a step at $s_2$, but its output weight is $-1$, so it's a step that goes down. Add the two together:

To the left of $s_1$ both are $0$, so th.zh: 在 $s_1$ 左侧两者都是 $0$，总和为 $0$。在 $s_1$ 与 $s_2$ 之间只有第一个起作用，总和保持在 $+1$。越过 $s_2$ 后下降阶跃开始生效，把它抵消回 $0$。剩下的就是一个@@T0@@凸包@@T1@@——两个阶跃之间的一小块平台。@@T2@@这就是我们的积木。@@T3@@
To the left of $s_1$ both are $0$, so th.src: To the left of $s_1$ both are $0$, so the total is $0$. Between $s_1$ and $s_2$ only the first is on, so the total sits at $+1$. After $s_2$ the down-step kicks in and cancels it back to $0$. What's left is a bump—a little plateau between the two steps. That's our brick.

Toggle the second neuron off and on to s.zh: 反复开闭第二个神经元，观察凸包如何出现与消失。拖动位置和权重。然后点击@@T0@@添加 sigmoid@@T1@@，再叠加若干个——你构造出的每条曲线都只是这些柔和阶跃之和。
Toggle the second neuron off and on to s.src: Toggle the second neuron off and on to see the bump appear and vanish. Drag the positions and weights. Then press Add sigmoid and stack a few more—every curve you build is just a sum of these soft steps.

Each @@T0@@dashed@@T1@@ curve is one\n.zh: 每条@@T0@@虚线@@T1@@曲线是一个 sigmoid 的贡献；@@T2@@橙色实线@@T3@@曲线是它们的总和。
Each @@T0@@dashed@@T1@@ curve is one\n.src: Each dashed curve is one sigmoid’s contribution; the solid orange curve is their sum.

@@T0@@Why subtraction is the trick.@@T1@.zh:
@@T0@@为何相减是关键。@@T1@@
          单个阶跃只能上升。两个阶跃——一个上升，稍后另一个下降——会在其间留下一块平坦的小岛。这块小岛正是我们唯一需要的形状：一个可移动、可拉伸、可翻转的凸包。
@@T0@@Why subtraction is the trick.@@T1@.src: Why subtraction is the trick. A single step can only go up. Two steps—one up, one down a little later—leave a flat island in between. That island is the only shape we'll ever need: a movable, stretchable, flippable bump.

Chop $[0, 1]$ into $N$ adjacent slabs an.zh: 把 $[0, 1]$ 切成 $N$ 个相邻的区间，在每个区间上放一个凸包。隐藏层的输出便成为一排相互独立的平台——第 $i$ 个凸包在第 $i$ 个区间上贡献其高度：
Chop $[0, 1]$ into $N$ adjacent slabs an.src:
Chop $[0, 1]$ into $N$ adjacent slabs and drop one bump on each. The
          hidden layer's output becomes a row of independent plateaus—bump
          $i$ contributes its height on slab $i$:

Each slider below is one bump's height..zh: 下面的每个滑块对应一个凸包的高度。浅色的阴影块就是凸包本身；@@T0@@蓝色@@T1@@线是网络沿各凸包顶端行进时实际输出的结果。调整各条形以描出@@T2@@橙色@@T3@@目标曲线——然后增加区间数目以获得更精细的拟合。
Each slider below is one bump's height..src: Each slider below is one bump's height. The faint shaded blocks are the bumps themselves; the blue line is what the network actually outputs as it rides along their tops. Set the bars to trace the orange target—then add more slabs for a finer trace.

Try it by hand, or hit @@T0@@Auto-fit@@T.zh: 你可以手工调节，也可以点击@@T0@@自动拟合@@T1@@让每个条形对齐目标。然后增大 $N$，观察阶梯如何变密。
Try it by hand, or hit @@T0@@Auto-fit@@T.src: Try it by hand, or hit Auto-fit to snap every bar to the target. Then drag $N$ up and watch the staircase tighten.

@@T0@@Orange@@T1@@: target.\n.zh:
@@T0@@橙色@@T1@@：目标。
            @@T2@@蓝色@@T3@@：你手工构建的输出。

@@T0@@More bumps, smaller gap.@@T1@@\n.zh:
@@T0@@凸包越多，差距越小。@@T1@@
          增大 $N$ 并重新拟合。阶梯变得更细密，偏差趋于零。整个定理就浓缩在这一个滑块里：@@T2@@精度是用宽度换来的。@@T3@@
@@T0@@More bumps, smaller gap.@@T1@@\n.src: More bumps, smaller gap. Crank $N$ up and re-fit. The staircase gets finer and the deviation shrinks toward zero. That's the entire theorem in one slider: accuracy is bought with width.

One small wrinkle &mdash; safe to skip.zh: 一个小的细节——可以跳过
One small wrinkle &mdash; safe to skip.src: One small wrinkle — safe to skip

You may have noticed the bars don't sit.zh: 你可能已经注意到，各条形所在的高度与目标并不完全一致。原因一句话即可说清：真正的输出神经元会把凸包的总和再通过@@T0@@一个 sigmoid@@T1@@压缩一次。因此，若想让最终答案落在比如 $0.8$ 上，凸包瞄准的并不是 $0.8$——它们瞄准的是经过压缩后@@T2@@恰好变成@@T3@@ $0.8$ 的那个值。该值记作 $\sigma^{-1}(0.8)$，读作“sigma 逆”，意思就是@@T4@@把 sigmoid 反解@@T5@@。
You may have noticed the bars don't sit.src: You may have noticed the bars don't sit at exactly the same heights as the target. Here's why, in one breath: a real output neuron takes the bumps' total and squishes it through one more sigmoid. So to make the final answer land on, say, $0.8$, the bumps don't aim for $0.8$—they aim for the value that becomes $0.8$ after the squish. That value is written $\sigma^{-1}(0.8)$, read “sigma-inverse,” and it just means undo the sigmoid.

The same target before and after &ldquo;.zh: 同一目标在“解压缩”前后的对比。紫色虚线 $\sigma^{-1}(f)$ 正是凸包暗中瞄准的对象——它不过是把目标拉伸开来。
The same target before and after &ldquo;.src:
The same target before and after “un-squishing.” The
              dashed purple curve, $\sigma^{-1}(f)$, is what the bumps secretly
              aim at—it's just the target, stretched out.

You never have to think about this to us.zh: 使用上面的工具时你完全不必考虑这一点。但如果你点击@@T0@@“预览：未经压缩的目标”@@T1@@，绘图区就会切换到那个被拉伸的世界——在那里，凸包确实可以@@T2@@直接相加@@T3@@得到目标，不受压缩干扰。
You never have to think about this to us.src: You never have to think about this to use the tool above. But if you press “Peek: the un-squished goal,” the plot switches to that stretched-out world—and there the bumps literally add up to the goal, no squishing in the way.

So far: bricks on a line.zh: 到目前为止：直线上的积木
So far: bricks on a line.src: So far: bricks on a line

Pause and take stock. We turned a neuron.zh: 先暂停并梳理一下。我们把一个神经元变成了阶跃，把两个阶跃变成了凸包，又把一排凸包变成了任意想要的一维曲线。配方是：@@T0@@把输入切成区间，在每个区间上竖起一个高度合适的凸包。@@T1@@
Pause and take stock. We turned a neuron.src: Pause and take stock. We turned a neuron into a step, two steps into a bump, and a row of bumps into any 1-D curve we like. The recipe was: chop the input into slabs, raise a bump to the right height on each.

Now we want functions of @@T0@@two@@T1@@.zh: 现在我们要处理@@T0@@两个@@T1@@输入的函数——即地面上每个点对应一个高度，也就是一个曲面。方案完全相同，但我们的积木必须变成@@T2@@塔块@@T3@@：在地面的某个小方块上高耸、在其他各处平坦的形状。构造这个塔块是整个论证中唯一真正巧妙的一步，因此我们慢慢来。
Now we want functions of @@T0@@two@@T1@@.src: Now we want functions of two inputs—a height for every point on a floor, i.e. a surface. The plan is exactly the same, but our brick has to become a tower: something that's tall in one little square of the floor and flat everywhere else. Building that tower is the one genuinely clever step in the whole argument, so we'll take it slowly.

Two inputs: build a tower, step by step.zh: 两个输入：逐步构造一个塔块
Two inputs: build a tower, step by step.src: Two inputs: build a tower, step by step

With two inputs $x$ and $y$, a neuron's.zh: 有了两个输入 $x$ 与 $y$，神经元的“阶跃”就变成一堵@@T0@@墙@@T1@@：它只关注 $x$，因此是一道沿 $y$ 方向一直延伸的悬崖。观察下面四个面板——它们与之前是同一套构造，只是被抬高到三维。拖动任意滑块，四个面板会同步更新。@@T2@@拖动任意面板可使其旋转@@T3@@（或使用“旋转”滑块），环视整个构造。
With two inputs $x$ and $y$, a neuron's.src: With two inputs $x$ and $y$, a neuron's “step” becomes a wall: it only listens to $x$, so it's a cliff running all the way along $y$. Watch the four panels below—they're the same construction as before, just lifted into 3-D. Drag any slider; all four update together. Drag any panel to orbit it (or use the Rotate slider) and look around the build.

@@T0@@1. Wall.@@T1@@ One step in $x$ &md.zh: @@T0@@1. 墙。@@T1@@ 在 $x$ 方向上的一个阶跃——一道悬崖。
@@T0@@1. Wall.@@T1@@ One step in $x$ &md.src: 1. Wall. One step in $x$ — a cliff.

@@T0@@2. Ridge.@@T1@@ Two steps subtract.zh: @@T0@@2. 脊。@@T1@@ 两个阶跃相减——$x$ 方向上的一个凸包，形成一条长长的墙顶。
@@T0@@2. Ridge.@@T1@@ Two steps subtract.src: 2. Ridge. Two steps subtracted — a bump in $x$, a long wall-top.

@@T0@@3. Cross.@@T1@@ Add a ridge in $x$.zh: @@T0@@3. 十字。@@T1@@ 把 $x$ 方向的脊与 $y$ 方向的脊相加。重叠处堆叠到高度 $2h$，两臂处为 $h$。
@@T0@@3. Cross.@@T1@@ Add a ridge in $x$.src: 3. Cross. Add a ridge in $x$ and a ridge in $y$. They pile to height $2h$ where they overlap, $h$ on the arms.

@@T0@@4. Tower.@@T1@@ Pass the cross thr.zh: @@T0@@4. 塔块。@@T1@@ 让该十字再经过一个 sigmoid，其@@T2@@阈值@@T3@@取在 $h$ 与 $2h$ 之间。只有 $2h$ 的重叠部分得以保留。
@@T0@@4. Tower.@@T1@@ Pass the cross thr.src: 4. Tower. Pass the cross through one more sigmoid with a threshold between $h$ and $2h$. Only the $2h$ overlap survives.

@@T0@@1 · Wall (one step in x)@@T1@@.zh: @@T0@@1 · 墙（$x$ 方向的一个阶跃）@@T1@@

Brighter and taller = higher value. Slid.zh: 越亮、越高表示取值越大。把@@T0@@阈值@@T1@@从 $0.5h$ 调到 $2h$，观察面板 3 中的十字如何塌缩为面板 4 中干净的塔块。
Brighter and taller = higher value. Slid.src: Brighter and taller = higher value. Slide the threshold from $0.5h$ up to $2h$ and watch the cross in panel 3 collapse into the clean tower in panel 4.

@@T0@@Why threshold at $1.5h$?@@T1@@\n.zh:
@@T0@@为何阈值取 $1.5h$？@@T1@@
          这是唯一能把“两条脊同时开启”（$2h$）与“只有一条开启”（$h$）区分开的水平。阈值设得过低，脊的两臂会漏过而形成十字形状；设得过高，连中心都会被削掉。当你@@T2@@只@@T3@@保留重叠部分时，剩下的就是塔块。
@@T0@@Why threshold at $1.5h$?@@T1@@\n.src: Why threshold at $1.5h$? It's the only level that separates “both ridges on” ($2h$) from “just one” ($h$). Set the threshold too low and the ridge arms leak through into a plus-shape; too high and even the center dies. The tower is what's left when you keep only the overlap.

Tile towers into any surface.zh: 平铺塔块以构造任意曲面

A tower is a movable, resizable block of.zh: 塔块是一个可移动、可缩放、高度可调的方块。用一网格这样的方块铺满地面，并把每个塔块的高度设为目标曲面在该处的取值。其总和构成一个贴合曲面的三维“阶梯”——与一维情形一样，网格越细，拟合越接近。这就是两个输入下的通用逼近，而同样的做法可平铺到任意多个输入。
A tower is a movable, resizable block of.src:
A tower is a movable, resizable block of adjustable height. Cover the
          floor with a grid of them and set each tower's height to the value of
          the target surface at that spot. The sum is a 3-D
          “staircase” that hugs the surface—and just like in
          1-D, a finer grid means a closer fit. That's universal approximation
          for two inputs, and the same move tiles into any number of inputs.

The @@T0@@Single spike@@T1@@ target make.zh: @@T0@@单尖峰@@T1@@目标让塔块很容易辨认——它们堆成一座小小的阶梯金字塔。增大@@T2@@分辨率@@T3@@以增加塔块，观察各方块如何收缩并逼近光滑目标。@@T4@@拖动曲面可使其旋转@@T5@@（或使用“旋转”滑块），欣赏这幅天际线。
The @@T0@@Single spike@@T1@@ target make.src: The Single spike target makes the towers easy to see—they stack into a little stepped pyramid. Drag resolution up to add towers and watch the blocks shrink toward the smooth target. Drag a surface to orbit it (or use the Rotate slider) and admire the skyline.

Same colours and heights on both. The ri.zh: 两幅图的颜色与高度完全一致。右侧曲面完全由 sigmoid 塔块堆成——提高分辨率，天际线便会融入目标。
Same colours and heights on both. The ri.src:
Same colours and heights on both. The right surface is built
            entirely from sigmoid towers—raise the resolution and the
            skyline melts into the target.

@@T0@@Count the cost.@@T1@@\n E.zh:
@@T0@@算一算代价。@@T1@@
          每个塔块需要 $4$ 个隐藏神经元（两条脊 × 两个阶跃）。$7\times7$ 的网格就是 $49$ 个塔块——$196$ 个神经元——而这只是粗糙的拟合。把分辨率推高，神经元数量会急剧膨胀。这个定理保证拟合@@T2@@存在@@T3@@；它从未承诺这会是廉价的。
@@T0@@Count the cost.@@T1@@\n E.src: Count the cost. Each tower needs $4$ hidden neurons (two ridges × two steps). A $7\times7$ grid is $49$ towers—$196$ neurons—for a coarse fit. Push the resolution up and the neuron count explodes. The theorem guarantees a fit exists; it never promised it would be cheap.

You've now built the whole argument with.zh: 至此你已用自己的双手搭建了完整论证：阶跃 → 凸包 → 设计的曲线 → 塔块 → 平铺曲面。这确实是对通用性的一个证明。但当它被压缩成一句口号时，有四件事悄然丢失了：
You've now built the whole argument with.src:
You've now built the whole argument with your own hands: step →
          bump → designed curve → tower → tiled surface. It's
          genuinely a proof of universality. But four things quietly get lost
          when it's flattened into a slogan:

@@T0@@&ldquo;One hidden layer is enough.zh:
@@T0@@“在实践中一个隐藏层就够了。”@@T1@@@@T2@@
              原则上，足够的@@T3@@宽度@@T4@@确实够用——但这个宽度可能高得离谱。我们的平铺方式每个塔块花掉 $4$ 个神经元，拟合结果仍然呈块状。@@T5@@深度@@T6@@使网络能够用凸包构建凸包、复用部件，这正是真实网络选择加深而非荒谬地加宽的原因。
@@T0@@&ldquo;One hidden layer is enough.src:
“One hidden layer is enough in practice.”
Enough width suffices in principle—but the width can be astronomical. Our tiling spent $4$ neurons per tower and still gave a blocky fit. Depth lets a network build bumps from bumps and reuse parts, which is why real networks are deep, not absurdly wide.

@@T0@@&ldquo;Training will find this net.zh:
@@T0@@“训练会找到这个网络。”@@T1@@@@T2@@
              我们每一个阶跃和高度都是@@T3@@手工摆放@@T4@@的。该证明说明存在一个好的网络@@T5@@@@T6@@；但对梯度下降能否发现它则只字未提。存在性与可学习性是两个不同的问题。
@@T0@@&ldquo;Training will find this net.src:
“Training will find this network.”
We placed every step and height by hand. The proof shows a good network exists; it's silent on whether gradient descent can discover it. Existence and learnability are different questions.

@@T0@@&ldquo;Sigmoids are special.&rdquo.zh:
@@T0@@“sigmoid 是特殊的。”@@T1@@@@T2@@
              这里的任何环节都不特别依赖 sigmoid——任何能够起到阶跃作用的非线性激活函数（对 ReLU 而言则是折角）都可以。S 形曲线只是让阶跃的图像更直观而已。
@@T0@@&ldquo;Sigmoids are special.&rdquo.src:
“Sigmoids are special.”
Nothing here needs the sigmoid in particular—any non-linear activation that can act like a step (or a hinge, for ReLU) works. The S-curve just made the step picture vivid.

@@T0@@&ldquo;It means networks generaliz.zh:
@@T0@@“这意味着网络能够泛化。”@@T1@@@@T2@@
              该构造只在你所平铺的区域上拟合目标——它关乎函数的@@T3@@表示@@T4@@，而非在新输入上预测良好。泛化是另一个由数据和归纳偏置所讲述的故事。
@@T0@@&ldquo;It means networks generaliz.src:
“It means networks generalize.”
The construction fits the target on the region you tile—it's about representing a function, not predicting well on new inputs. Generalization is a separate story told by data and inductive bias.

@@T0@@Final takeaway.@@T1@@\n &.zh:
@@T0@@最后总结。@@T1@@
          “通用”意味着，只要把单个隐藏层中的凸包摆放得当，就能以任意接近的程度匹配任何连续函数。你并没有凭信念接受这一点——你亲手压平了 sigmoid、粘合了凸包、堆叠了塔块。现代深度学习的艺术在于@@T2@@高效地@@T3@@完成同样的事情：借助深度、优秀的优化器以及恰当的归纳偏置。
@@T0@@Final takeaway.@@T1@@\n &.src: Final takeaway. “Universal” means a single hidden layer of bumps can be arranged to match any continuous function as closely as you like. You didn't take that on faith—you flattened the sigmoids, glued the bumps, and stacked the towers yourself. The art of modern deep learning is doing the same thing efficiently: with depth, good optimizers, and the right inductive biases.

meta.title: 一层网络能够计算任意函数的可视化证明
meta.tagline: 把 sigmoid 压成阶跃、粘出凸包、堆起塔块——Nielsen 的通用性可视化证明，做成交互式
meta.summary: 亲手重建 Michael Nielsen 对通用逼近定理的可视化证明：把 sigmoid 调成阶跃，两个阶跃相减得到凸包，堆叠凸包以设计一维曲线，再逐步构造塔块并在可旋转的三维曲面上平铺塔块。
highlights: 观察 sigmoid 如何突变为阶跃函数，并学习 Nielsen 按阶跃位置 s = -b/w 的重参数化。
两个阶跃相减得到凸包，再用一组各凸包高度滑块设计出整条函数——包括输出 sigmoid 所隐藏的 σ⁻¹∘f 细节。
逐步构造二维塔块（墙、脊、十字、阈值），并在可旋转的三维曲面上平铺塔块以逼近任意函数，观察天际线随分辨率提高而变锐利。

step at s = [[[0]]].zh: 位于 s = [[[0]]] 处的阶跃
